rules.statement: Don't report reading properties through a resolved object's options data holder (such as `frontend.Options.TrustedOrigins`) as a call-chain or Law-of-Demeter violation; that rule targets chains of collaborator method calls like `a.B().C().D()`, not property reads on a plain options/data object.
rules.why: Copying every setting from the options type onto the owning type would duplicate the options class and weaken cohesion; property reads on a data holder are not the coupling the rule warns about.
rules.check: Before reporting a member-access chain, check whether the intermediate is a data holder (options/record) being read for properties rather than a collaborator whose methods are called in a chain.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't report a local test helper as duplicating a shared helper when it calls the shared helper and only adds settings on top of it.
rules.why: A helper that delegates to the shared one repeats no defaults, so changes to the shared defaults already reach it and it cannot drift.
rules.check: Read the body of the supposedly duplicate helper; if it calls the shared helper (e.g. with a configure callback) and only adds settings, don't raise the finding.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't ask to move a stub or fake that only one test file needs out of that file; the test conventions make it a `private sealed` nested type of that test class, which is an allowed exception to the no-nested-types rule.
rules.why: The test isolation conventions explicitly require a single-file stub to be a private sealed nested type in that file.
rules.check: Before reporting a nested type in a test class, check whether it is a private sealed stub used only in that file; if so, don't report it.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't report `null!` when it passes a deliberate null to the code under test to check an argument-null guard; the test conventions allow that use of the null-forgiving operator.
rules.why: The C# and test conventions sanction `null!` in test projects for argument-validation tests, so the ban on postfix `!` doesn't apply there.
rules.check: Before reporting `null!` in a test, check whether it is an argument passed to the code under test in a null-guard/argument-validation test; only report other uses.

rules.statement: An options validator (`IValidateOptions<T>`) must report a duplicate registration, such as the same rule or name registered twice, as a validation failure instead of throwing from its constructor.
rules.why: A constructor exception surfaces as a raw composition error, while a validation failure names the configuration key and fits the options-validation pipeline.
rules.check: Look for `throw` statements in an options validator's constructor, or duplicate detection done outside `Validate`, and ask for it to become a `ValidateOptionsResult` failure.

rules.statement: In a test project, every test must assert the behavior its name claims; a test that only constructs objects and asserts nothing must be given an explicit assertion (for example a strict mock showing a dependency is not touched until first use) or deleted.
rules.why: A test with no assertion has unclear intent and proves nothing, such as the laziness it claims.
rules.check: Look for test methods with no Assert, no mock verification and no expected-exception check.

rules.statement: Source files must stay UTF-8 without a byte-order mark; don't let a change add a BOM to a file.
rules.why: Adding a BOM changes the file's encoding for no reason.
rules.check: Look in the diff for a BOM (U+FEFF) added before line 1 of a file.

rules.statement: In a test project, every Moq setup ends with `.Verifiable()`, including value-stub setups (`SetupGet(...).Returns(...)`) on loose mocks.
rules.why: The maintainer confirmed that every setup must be verifiable; loose-mock value stubs are not exempt.
rules.check: Look for `Setup`/`SetupGet`/`SetupSequence` chains in tests that do not end with `.Verifiable()`.

rules.statement: Options validation failure messages must use one consistent format that starts with the full configuration key path of the member they are about (such as `Section:Item:Member must ...`), without placing a `: ` separator inside the key path.
rules.why: Inconsistent message formats confuse readers, and the tests end up pinning the odd form.
rules.check: Compare new validation messages with the existing ones in the same validator for key-path and separator format.

rules.statement: The PR description and changelog must describe the behavior the code actually implements (for example, which cases are ignored and which are refused with a given error), and must be corrected when they diverge.
rules.why: A reader comparing the description with the code is misled when they disagree.
rules.check: Compare the claims in the PR description and changelog with the code paths in the diff.
